questions.question_text: **[Stacks]** Briefly define a stack and state its primary characteristic.
questions.answer_key: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last‑In‑First‑Out (LIFO) principle. The primary characteristic is that the most recently added element is the first one to be removed.

questions.question_text: **[Queues]** Explain how a queue can be used to implement a round‑robin scheduling mechanism. Include in your answer the steps for adding new tasks and selecting the next task to run.
questions.answer_key:
Marking Scheme (2 marks total):
- 1 mark: Correct description of a queue as a First‑In‑First‑Out (FIFO) structure and how tasks are enqueued when they arrive.
- 1 mark: Clear explanation of the round‑robin cycle – the scheduler dequeues the task at the front, gives it a time‑slice, and if the task is not finished it is enqueued again at the rear. The process repeats, ensuring each task gets an equal share of CPU time.
Full credit requires both parts and appropriate terminology (enqueue, dequeue, FIFO, time‑slice).
